FINAL: <pass|issues> evidence=<ev-list>
```

## Resume

```
if last line does not match header|start|verdict|ruling|retry|halt|FINAL regex → E-LEDGER-CORRUPT
parse lines in order
for each id in T1..TN (source order):
  if no line for id → resume here
  if latest status for id is not complete → resume here
  if latest status is complete → skip
first such id wins
if all complete → run FINAL unless --skip-final-review or FINAL already present or N=1
```

The completion rules in this section are **legacy-ledger** rules; managed packages follow the Managed-package extension below.

`--resume` is implicit when a matching ledger exists. If the ledger is missing, write the header before the first edit. If all tasks are `complete` **and** FINAL is already present (or N=1, or `--skip-final-review`): STOP `already complete: <ledger path>`. If all tasks are `complete` and FINAL is still due: run FINAL, then stop. Do not skip a pending N>1 whole-list review.

Trust ledger + git history after compaction. Do not ask the user to paste prior chat.

### Per-task resume table

Definitions, over the task's records after its latest `start`: "Last record" = the last task record, ignoring ineligible Rulings. "Latest verdict" = the last `complete` or `blocked` line. A `T<id>: Ruling:` line is eligible only under the Ruling eligibility rule in `refs/retry.md`. Before any row except Row 1 runs for a task with a tree `start`, every `r<k>-<j>` ref of the task is re-pinned from its recorded tree (review header or repair `applied tree=` line, `refs/qa.md`), so Rows V, S, H, B and X re-pin as well.

Ledgers written before the change resume through the existing rows. Findings with no recorded tree get `origin=unknown`, and absent repair files for the current `start` mean no repair is spent.

Precondition: one `/sc:implement` invocation writes a given ledger at a time; there is no lock.

Task selection stays as the pseudo-code above; this table replaces only the per-task dispatch (the "resume here" step). The table applies to legacy and managed ledgers alike: the completion rules above are scoped to legacy ledgers, so the managed dispatch line below ("first non-complete task") routes to this table. In every row, k is the k-rule value (`refs/retry.md`).

First match wins; the row order is part of the rule:

| Row | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Latest verdict is `complete` | Skip. Delete the Q0 pin and checkpoint refs if they still exist; keep sweep refs. Also delete the task's `r<k>-<j>` refs. |
| R | An eligible Ruling with no `complete` after it | Append the post-ruling `complete` with the latest `blocked` line's verdict unchanged (Post-ruling complete line), with no review, then row 1. |
| P | Latest verdict is `blocked`, and the task has no `retry` and no `halt` record | One fresh operator review of the tree as it stands, nothing reverted. `compliant` → `complete`. Otherwise append `blocked` and `halt review=2 reason=operator-review` → STOP `E-HALT-QA`. |
| H | A `halt` record exists | If the last record is a `blocked` after the latest `halt`, append `halt review=<k> reason=<r>` with r = `operator-review` → STOP. Otherwise one fresh operator review of the tree as it stands: `compliant` → `complete`; else `blocked`, then `halt review=<k> reason=<r>` with r = `operator-review` → STOP `E-HALT-QA`. |
| V | Last record is `retry n=<n> step=review` | If a `repair-<n>-<j>.md` for the current `start` exists, resume the repair (`refs/retry.md`, Repair round). Otherwise: Re-run only the review of attempt n (fresh reviewer). `compliant` → Q6-Q8; otherwise the Repair round decides as an uninterrupted run would, then procedure step 0 with k = n. |
| X | Last record is `retry n=<n> step=revert` | Run `sc_retry_revert` directly: its ledger binding and guards (tail, tree, HEAD, evidence) are the re-check, and exit 2 maps to the halt after any move-back or keep of failed-attempt artifacts (`refs/retry.md`, The revert). Otherwise the revert re-runs (idempotent: fresh `now`, create-only sweep), then procedure step 7. |
| O | Last record is `retry n=<n> step=open` | Re-check the ladder conditions (`refs/retry.md`, When the ladder runs), re-pin the checkpoint ref to the recorded sha and every `r<k>-<j>` ref from its recorded tree, then continue at procedure step 2. n = 3, 4: advisers re-spawned (procedure step 4). n = 5: escalation 3 runs again (no adviser; `T<id>_brief-5.md` rewritten). |
| B | Last record is a `blocked` line and the task has a `retry` record | k from the k rule (here the n of the latest `retry`, because this `blocked` follows its `step=review`). k = 5 → append `halt review=5 reason=ladder-end` → STOP. Otherwise continue at the ladder-condition checks for this k, then procedure step 1. |
| S | Start line only | If a `repair-2-<j>.md` for the current `start` exists, resume the repair (`refs/retry.md`, Repair round). Else A1, as today. |

Managed ledgers (`<package>/progress.md`) reuse every record above unchanged and add three record kinds. Legacy ledgers never contain them.

# Spec-compliance rubric

Loaded for Q3–Q5. Do not load reflect-protocol. Do not re-run the full test suite as the review.

## Reviewer contract

Do not trust the implementer's report.

Input is the task brief (Ti text + AC ids + global constraints) and the diff (`git diff "$start"` vs the Q0 snapshot, plus full contents of untracked files in the touched set, or tool-trace paths if `nogit`). Not "the tests passed". An empty git diff with new untracked writes is not `cannot-verify`.

One reviewer per review; never 2+ reviewer agents for the same review. No Part 2 code-quality ensemble. No `/sc:reflect`. No 6-agent panel.

## Compare the diff to

- that task's AC (`Ti.ACk`) — for informal/prompt sources this is the source text itself; extra comes only from a confirmed `harmful-effect` or `quoted-constraint-breach` finding
- parent spec constraints (`## Constraints` / `## Out of scope` / `## Non-goals` / `## Non-negotiable`)
- explicit instructions on the task ("do not X", "file Y only")

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Missing | AC/instruction not in the diff, with a confirmed B1 or B2 finding |
| Extra | behavior/files/API the brief did not ask for, with a confirmed B3 or B4 finding |
| Misunderstood | work present but solves the wrong thing |

## Citations

For each AC of Ti, cite `path:line` in the produced diff (or `Ti.ACk@path:line`).

Every AC mark, met or unmet, carries a `path:line` or `Ti.ACk@path:line` citation, and an `unmet` mark also lists the finding ids behind it. This rule is part of the Verdict owner correction below (a deliberate SPEC correction). A bare `Ti.ACk` is not sufficient evidence for `compliant`.

Invalid evidence: `the component works`, `tests pass`, `as implemented above`, line-less paths, a bare `Ti.ACk` on a `compliant` line, citations into files not in this task's touched set unless the AC required reading them (then cite the source spec `path:line`).

A verdict with **zero citations** is invalid → treat as `cannot-verify`.

## Severity model

Every finding has exactly one severity, derived by the parent from the finding's checklist answers, never read from the reviewer's wording:

| Severity | Definition |
|---|---|
| `blocking` | At least one checklist answer is `yes` and its anchor passed the parent's Read-back, and the inherited cap (text with origin `inherited`) does not apply. |
| `minor` | All four answers are `no`, and the finding is a real defect in what this task delivered: ambiguous wording, a missing or mismatched evidence entry for a claim the reviewer verified true, including a citation or copied value that only drifted (Line-drift boundary below). |
| `note` | All four answers are `no`, and the finding is cosmetic, a "consider changing" suggestion, or has origin `inherited` or `late`; also any finding whose only `yes` failed its Read-back. |

**Four checklist answers; the blocking triggers.** Every finding carries four factual answers, each `yes` or `no`. Each answer is the confirmation of one blocking trigger, so the trigger names stay as a glossary:

| Answer | Trigger | `yes` when |
|---|---|---|
| `ac-outcome-missing` | B1 unmet AC | Output an AC requires is absent, or contradicts the AC text, or an evidence claim the reviewer could not verify has no evidence row (Evidence-type AC). |
| `false-claim` | B2 wrong statement | A claim in delivered text or code is false against live source, a recipe or instruction followed as written does not do what the text says it does, or a span an earlier review accepted is later shown false. |
| `harmful-effect` | B3 harmful effect | Code or a recipe added or changed by this task writes, appends, chmods or deletes tracked or production data, mutates state outside the task's declared outputs, or exposes a secret. |
| `quoted-constraint-breach` | B4 constraint breach | The diff violates a parent `## Constraints` / `## Out of scope` / `## Non-goals` / `## Non-negotiable` item or an explicit task instruction ("## Compare the diff to" above), including editing text the plan reserves for another task, and the reviewer can quote that text. |

"Cannot verify" (formerly B5) is not a per-finding severity. It stays the existing `cannot-verify` step of the verdict order ("## Verdict (exactly one)"); an evidence claim the reviewer could not verify is `ac-outcome-missing=yes` anchored on the AC words.

**Who assigns severity.** The reviewer answers the four questions and cites one anchor per `yes`. The parent orchestrator then derives the severity mechanically and Reads each anchor back once:

- `ac-outcome-missing`: the quoted AC words are byte-present in the AC, and the Verified-minor rule below does not apply.
- `false-claim`: the cited live-source `path:line` holds the contradicting text; an anchor that shows only drift is handled by the Line-drift boundary below, which sets the answer to `no`.
- `harmful-effect`: the cited diff line is the write.
- `quoted-constraint-breach`: the quoted text is byte-present in the plan Constraints or a task instruction.

**Verified-minor rule (parent-side).** An `ac-outcome-missing` answer fails its Read-back when all of these hold:

- an earlier review of the current tree chain (all reviews since the task's `start` or its latest revert, as in the notes rule) has a notes-file finding line with all four answers `no` (`minor` or `note`) on the same path and the same `ac=` as the new finding, and that `ac=` is an AC that asks for evidence (Evidence-type AC below);
- the line that notes line cites, as it stands in that review's pinned tree (the `r<k>-<j>` on the notes line), is not blank and is byte-identical to the new finding's flagged line (`at=`) in the tree under review;
- every path that the flagged line cites or the AC text names, and that exists in that pinned tree, still exists in the tree under review. An evidence artifact a later change removed stays `ac-outcome-missing=yes` ("the evidence artifact is absent", Evidence-type AC below);
- that pinned tree exists. With `tree=none`, a missing ref or a notes line without `ac=`, the rule does not apply and the answer is read back as usual.

That earlier review answered `ac-outcome-missing=no` on the same unchanged text (for an evidence claim, it verified the claim true), so a later review that could not verify it cannot turn it into a blocker. The parent checks this from the notes file and the pinned trees only. A `false-claim`, `harmful-effect` or `quoted-constraint-breach` answer on that text is not affected and blocks when its anchor passes.

**Line-drift boundary (parent-side).** A `false-claim` answer counts as `no` in the derivation when one of these string tests shows that only a pointer or a copied value in the delivered text went stale:

- Moved line: the earliest pinned reviewed tree (`r<k>-<j>`) that holds the delivered citation is earlier than the tree under review; the line the citation names in that earlier tree is not blank, holds the citation's quote when it has one, appears exactly once in that file in the earlier tree, is no longer at the cited line number, and appears exactly once, at another line, in the same file in the tree under review. With `tree=none`, a missing ref, a citation present in `$start`, or a citation that first appears in the tree under review, this test does not apply.
- Copied log value: the anchor is a line of a saved log or command-output file and the delivered text quotes part of it; once every run of digits is replaced by one placeholder, the quote is a substring of the anchor line; no number in the quote changes between zero and non-zero; and no number on the anchor line on either side of `failed`, `failures`, `error` or `errors` (in any case, `word=N` included) is non-zero. A delivered `989 passed` against a log line `=== 990 passed, 3 warnings in 1.2s ===` qualifies; `0 failed` against `2 failed`, and `989 passed` against `1 failed, 989 passed`, do not. This test never applies when the number itself is what an AC asks for.

Such a finding, with no other `yes`, is a mismatched evidence entry for a verified-true claim: all-`no` and `minor`. Any other difference (a changed word, a pass that became a fail, a number that crosses zero, a citation that fails either test) is contradicting text, and the answer stays `yes`. These are file and string comparisons, not a judgment; there is no second model pass.

A finding whose only `yes` fails its Read-back is a note. The reviewer's prose label (low, IMPORTANT, MINOR or any other) is never read. There is no second model pass: one reviewer per review ("## Reviewer contract"), and the Read-back is a file check, not a judgment.

**Derivation and vocabulary mapping.** Any confirmed `yes` gives `blocking`, except that a finding on inherited text is capped at note by the inherited cap. All `no` gives `minor`, or `note` when the finding is cosmetic or its origin is `inherited` or `late`. Mapping of the words a reviewer might use: high = any confirmed checklist `yes` = `blocking`; medium, IMPORTANT without a `yes`, low-medium, low and cosmetic = `minor` or `note`.

**Evidence-type AC.** For an AC that asks for evidence, the AC is unmet only when:

- the evidence artifact is absent (`ac-outcome-missing=yes`);
- a cited evidence row is false (`false-claim=yes`; a row whose line or copied value only drifted is not false, Line-drift boundary above); or
- a claim the reviewer could not verify has no evidence row (`ac-outcome-missing=yes`, anchored on the AC words).

A claim the reviewer verified true but that lacks a row, a row for a verified-true claim whose cited line or copied value only drifted (Line-drift boundary above), and a saved script/output pair that does not match when the reviewer reproduced the claim itself, are all-`no` findings: `minor`. The reviewer may not widen the AC (for example from "each corrected behavior" to "every sentence asserting a fact").

**Fix cost and the ponytail lens.** The fix-cost question ("is the fix worth its lines") lives in the `fix=` field of every finding. Over-engineering observations are notes. A ponytail-style judgment never changes a checklist answer, so it never changes a severity or a verdict; never deletes or shrinks text an AC requires; and never reduces the set of sites a family probe listed (it may pick the smaller fix per listed site). The protocol never invokes the `ponytail-review` plugin, so its absence changes nothing.

**Precedence over the output style.** Inside `/sc:implement` this protocol severity model governs per-task QA and both FINALs (managed and legacy). This precedence covers the session's output style and the copy of it that the SubagentStart hook injects into every subagent, reviewers and advisers included: only `blocking` findings may fail an attempt, halt or prompt the user.

## Verdict owner (deliberate SPEC correction)

This rule is a deliberate SPEC correction of FR-006, which contradicts itself on who produces the verdict. The reviewer returns, per AC, `met` or `unmet`, each with a `path:line` or `Ti.ACk@path:line` citation; an `unmet` mark also lists the finding ids behind it; plus its finding lines, and no verdict. After the anchor Read-back, the origin fields and the inherited cap, the parent runs the closed order of "## Verdict (exactly one)" over the parent-confirmed blocking findings only and records the result as the verdict, once; nobody rewrites a recorded verdict.

- An AC counts as unmet only when a parent-confirmed B1 or B2 blocker is attached to it.
- A confirmed B1 or B2 finding with `ac=scope` is attached to every AC whose cited text or file it touches, or to every AC of the task when it touches none, so a review with any confirmed blocker never yields `compliant`.
- An `unmet` mark whose listed findings are all non-blocking after the Read-back and the inherited cap counts as met with its citation.
- Only an `unmet` mark that lists no finding, or a mark with no citation, is reviewer paperwork: the review is unparseable; respawn the reviewer once with the same input, and if that fails too, STOP `E-RESUME-NEEDED reason=reviewer-down` (`refs/retry.md`).

## Verdict (exactly one)

Closed enum: `compliant` | `missing` | `extra` | `misunderstood` | `cannot-verify`.

No other strings. Not `pass`/`fail`/`issues`. Not `spec-compliant`.

Apply in this order:

1. if zero citations → `cannot-verify`
2. if diff empty and no ruling → `cannot-verify`
3. elif any unmet AC → `missing`
4. elif any misunderstood → `misunderstood` (dominates extra)
5. elif extra_scope nonempty → `extra`
6. else → `compliant` only if every met AC has a `path:line` or `Ti.ACk@path:line` citation; otherwise `cannot-verify`

If both missing and extra: verdict `missing`. Record extra findings on the same ledger line after the verdict.

`cannot-verify` is not a pass. Empty diff after "done" → `cannot-verify`. AC not observable from the diff and no check/log/test added → `cannot-verify`. `nogit` and no written-path list → `cannot-verify`.

Inputs to the order (the enum and the order are unchanged; only their inputs are the parent-confirmed findings):

- An AC is unmet only when a B1 or B2 finding is attached to it.
- `misunderstood` requires a B1 finding of the "contradicts" kind.
- `extra_scope` is non-empty only for B3 or B4 findings.
- An AC claim the reviewer cannot verify (formerly B5) gives `cannot-verify` through the existing order.
- `minor` and `note` findings never change the verdict. A review whose findings are all `minor` or `note` yields `compliant`, provided every met AC has a citation (step 6 above).
- An empty diff whose AC are all met by a cited live-source `path:line` is `compliant`; an empty diff without such a citation stays `cannot-verify`.

## Review file format

`<retries>/T<id>/review-<k>.md` starts with one header line holding the task's `start` sha and the 40-hex of the reviewed tree, then the reviewer's AC marks and citations verbatim, then one finding per line:

```
F<k>.<j> sev=<blocking|minor|note> trigger=<B1|B2|B3|B4|none> ac=<Ti.ACk|scope> at=<path:line> anchor=<quoted text or path:line> chk=<amiss,false,harm,constraint as y/n> family=<id> fix=<text> [covers=<quoted AC clause or constraint>] first=<start|A<m>> origin=<inherited|late|fix-induced|new|unknown>: <text>
```

- The reviewer writes `ac=`, `at=`, `anchor=`, `chk=`, `family=` (short, reviewer-chosen, reused for findings of the same defect form), `fix=`, the optional `covers=<quoted AC clause or constraint>` and the text. `covers=` is the escape from the inherited cap: the parent Reads it back like `quoted-constraint-breach`, and only a quote byte-present in the AC or the plan Constraints lifts the cap.
- The parent writes `sev=`, `trigger=`, `first=` and `origin=`; the reviewer never writes these four keys.
- There is no locality key on a finding: whether a fix is local is the parent's decision.
- The file also holds one status line per prior blocking finding: `F<m>.<j> resolved|open|regressed`.
- Finding ids: `j` counts reviews within attempt k. A re-review inside attempt k continues the j numbering of the earlier reviews of attempt k, so a finding id `F<k>.<j>` is never reused within a task.

When it is written: the parent writes `review-<k>.md` as soon as a review of attempt k returns with a confirmed blocking finding (k = 1 for the A1 review, k = 2 to 5 otherwise), before any fix, repair or procedure step 0 of `refs/retry.md`: the header line, the reviewer's AC marks and citations verbatim, then the finding lines (reviewer keys and text verbatim, the four parent keys added). A later failing review of the same attempt overwrites it, so `review-<k>.md` is always the last failing review of attempt k. This file is not in the ledger, so no ledger regex parses it.

## Finding origin and first-seen attempt

For every finding the parent, never the reviewer, writes two fields into the review file, from exact line text:

- `first=<start|A<m>>`: the earliest pinned reviewed tree of this `start` (Pinned reviewed trees below) that holds the flagged text, or `start` when `$start` holds it.
- `origin=`:
  - `inherited`: the text is present in `$start`.
  - `late`: the text is present in an earlier reviewed tree of the current chain and was not flagged there. `late` takes precedence over `fix-induced`.
  - `fix-induced`: the text first appears in a tree written by an in-place fix (the A2 fix pass or a repair) after a review.
  - `new`: the first review of the chain, or text of a tree rebuilt from Q0 by an adviser brief, which starts a new chain.
  - `unknown`: `$start` is not a tree (HEAD fallback or `nogit`, the Q0 step of `SKILL.md`), or a recorded tree is missing.

"Not flagged there" means not flagged as a blocking finding: a text an earlier review flagged only as minor or note and a later review raises as a blocker is `late`, also when that earlier review file was overwritten, because origin reads only the pinned trees and the blocking finding lines kept in `review-*.md` and `repair-*.md`.

Handling by origin:

| Origin | Defined by (parent, exact line text) | Blocking finding | Non-blocking finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inherited` | text present in `$start` | capped at note, mechanically from the `git diff "$start"` hunk headers, unless a quoted AC clause or constraint covers it or a task-added sentence depends on it (`covers=`) | note |
| `late` | present in an earlier reviewed tree of the current chain and not flagged there | blocks at every attempt; never capped; never a regression | note |
| `fix-induced` | first present in a tree written by an in-place fix after a review | blocks, and is a regression only on an in-place-fix tree; sends the next step to the adviser route | minor, recorded; not edited from A3 |
| `new` | first review of the chain, or text of a Q0-rebuilt tree | blocks | minor or note per the derivation |
| `unknown` | `$start` not a tree, or a recorded tree missing | no origin rule applies; severity stands as derived | as derived |

The `covers=` escape is read from the reviewer's `covers=` key after its Read-back (Review file format above). A `fix-induced` blocker counts as a regression only on a tree produced by an in-place fix; text of a Q0-rebuilt tree is `new` and is never a regression. With no usable baseline (`unknown`) there is no inherited cap.

## Pinned reviewed trees and the `start` header

Origin needs every reviewed tree, including A1's and each repair's, and a repair writes no `step=open` checkpoint.

- Each reviewed tree is pinned as `refs/superclaude/implement/<slug>/retry/T<rid>/r<k>-<j>` (k = the attempt, 1 to 5; j = 1 for the attempt's first review and j+1 for the re-review after repair j), and its 40-hex is written on the header line of that review file.
- On any resume each `r<k>-<j>` ref is re-pinned from the tree on the header line of the review file that graded it, or, for the tree a repair produced, from the `applied tree=` line of that repair file (repair file format: Repair round in `refs/retry.md`).
- At `complete`, after `first=` and `origin=` are written, these refs are deleted with the checkpoint refs.
- Every `review-*.md`, `repair-*.md`, `probe-*.md`, `prompt-*.md` and notes file holds the task's `start` sha on its first line; a file holding any other value counts as absent.
- When `$start` is not a tree (`nogit` or HEAD fallback), no `r<k>-<j>` ref is pinned or re-pinned, the review header records `tree=none`, every origin is `unknown`, and a missing reviewed-tree ref is never `ref-failed`.

## What each review may raise

Every review at every attempt may raise a new blocker (any confirmed checklist `yes`) anywhere in task-owned text, meaning text the task added or changed; text present in `$start` follows the inherited rule above. A blocker on task-owned text is never capped, whatever its origin or attempt. Only new minors, notes and "cannot verify" findings with no confirmed `yes` on text unchanged since the last pinned reviewed tree are capped at note, so later reviews cannot re-open accepted text with a lower-severity finding. This cap also covers a "could not verify" `ac-outcome-missing` on text an earlier review of the current tree chain recorded as an all-`no` finding (`minor` or `note`): by the Verified-minor rule ("## Severity model") its `yes` fails the Read-back, so it is a note at every attempt and never becomes a `late` blocker. Minors and notes never fail an attempt.

| Review of | Scope of audit | Prior-finding re-check | Fails the attempt |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Full audit of the diff | none | a confirmed blocker only |
| A2 and each repair re-review | Full audit, plus the delta diff from the previous pinned reviewed tree as context | each prior blocking finding marked `resolved`, `open` or `regressed`; the saved-probe re-check list | a confirmed blocker only |
| A3 | as A2 | as A2 | a confirmed blocker only |
| A4 | as A2 | as A2 | a confirmed blocker only |
| A5 | as A2 | as A2 | a confirmed blocker only |

A non-blocking `late` finding is a note. A finding whose flagged text is absent from the current tree is `resolved` in the re-check, is not carried to notes, and keeps its recorded `first=` and `origin=`.

## Notes file and accepted-minor path

**Notes file.** The file is `<retries>/T<id>/notes.md`. Line 1 holds the task's `start` sha (see "Pinned reviewed trees and the `start` header"). Each finding line is `A<k> r<k>-<j> F<k>.<i> <minor|note> <path:line> ac=<Ti.ACk|scope> <checklist answers> <text>`; the `r<k>-<j>` tag names the review that raised it. An answer that the Verified-minor rule or the Line-drift boundary ("## Severity model") set aside is written `n`, so both FINALs cite that entry `noted`. Each dispute line is `A<n> dispute (advice-<n>-<x>.md): F<k>.<i> <minor|note> <reason>` (written by the adviser-route dispute rule of procedure step 3 in `refs/retry.md`).

- The folder already exists for every tree-snapshot task, because Q0 writes `q0-head` there, and the revert domain excludes `<retries>`, so notes survive any revert. A task whose start is `nogit` or a HEAD fallback has no `q0-head`; it creates the folder when it first writes the file.
- Fail closed: if the file cannot be written, STOP `E-RESUME-NEEDED reason=ref-failed`, with no ledger line and no `blocked` line.

**Notes keep every minor of the final chain (deliberate SPEC correction of FR-020).** Every review that fails appends its `minor` and `note` findings to the notes file at once, tagged with its review id `r<k>-<j>`, before any later review can overwrite `review-<k>.md`. The passing review's minors and notes, and any capped finding of the final tree, are written at `complete`. The `complete` rewrite keeps, as lines 2 to m, every line of the current tree chain (all reviews since the latest Q0 rebuild, meaning since the task's `start` or its latest revert) whose flagged text is still in the final tree, plus every dispute line of the current `start`; every other line (lines of reverted trees and lines whose text is gone) follows line m, prefixed `superseded `. The `notes@` token cites lines 1 to m.

**Token rule.** A notes file holding any line after line 1 gets a `notes@<path>:1-<m>` token in `evidence=` on the `complete` line; a file holding only `superseded ` lines after line 1 gets the token `notes@<path>:1-1`; no file means no token. A review chain with no minors and no notes writes no notes file. The token is never an AC citation (`refs/ledger.md`).

**Automatic accepted-minor path.** When a review has no `blocking` finding, the orchestrator does three things and asks the user nothing:

1. Write the notes file (above).
2. Run Q6 extras.
3. Append the `complete verdict=compliant … notes@…` line (`refs/ledger.md`).

| | Accepted-minor | Ruling (Halt table above) |
|---|---|---|
| Who decides | Severity derived by the parent from the reviewer's checklist answers and anchors, plus the mechanical origin caps | The user, in the current conversation |
| Covers | `minor` and `note` only | Any explained gap, blockers included |
| Ledger | `compliant` verdict plus a `notes@` token | A `Ruling:` line, then `complete` with the unchanged non-compliant verdict |
| Writes a `Ruling:` line | Never | Always |

The Ruling path is unchanged and remains the only exit from a halt. Conditions on the accepted-minor path:

- A task completes with recorded minors only after a fresh subagent review (see "Subagent prompt").
- When no FINAL that can block will run (legacy N=1, legacy `--skip-final-review`, or any legacy run, whose FINAL is advisory), the run's final summary prints every recorded minor with its checklist answers. The summary is informational and never asks the user anything.
- A batch task whose A2 has only minor or note findings completes on this path instead of halting `batch`. A batch A2 with a confirmed blocker still halts `batch`.

## Family probe

Loaded with this file for the Q5 fix pass, so the probe exists before the first fix, not only on the retry ladder.

- Before any fix of a blocker (the Q5 fix pass, a repair, a brief run) the fixer writes the probe for every blocking family of the failing review that has no probe entry yet. The file is `<retries>/T<id>/probe-<k>-<j>.md`, named after the failing review `r<k>-<j>` whose families it covers, so the Q5 fix pass after the A1 review writes `probe-1-1.md`. When that file already exists, new families are appended to it; no probe file is overwritten, and the only in-place addition is the `after:` lines of an existing family entry. Line 1 is the `start` sha.
- Per family the entry holds: the defect form; one read-only search command; its before-output over the touched files plus the AC-named files; and the coupled sites (other lines in that scope that state or depend on the rule being fixed). These four make the entry complete for locality. After the fix, the fixer appends the after-output as `after:` lines under the same entry.
- Probe-pending counts only entries written since the latest Q0 rebuild (the task's `start` or its latest revert). After a revert, earlier entries are re-check items only.
- Probe-listed sibling and coupled edits are in scope; any other edit is extra scope. A missing or incomplete probe never stops the run: it makes that family non-local and becomes a reviewer re-check item.
- Probe command rule: the command is `grep` or `git grep` with literal arguments over the listed files, and its only options are `-n`, `-E`, `-F`, `-i`, `-w`, `-e <pattern>` and `--`. Every other option is refused, by name including `git grep -O` / `--open-files-in-pager` and `git grep --textconv`. `rg` is refused entirely, because ripgrep reads extra options, `--pre` included, from the file named by `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`. The parent checks the command before its first run and again before every re-run of a saved probe, including on resume; a probe that fails the check is never run and counts as missing.
- The orchestrator re-runs every saved probe before each later review and passes only hit locations to the reviewer as `{recheck_list}`, never as evidence that an AC is met.
- A fix that inserts the same block of 3 or more lines in 3 or more places adds a byte-equality probe naming one source copy.

## Halt table

| Verdict after Q4 (or after Q5 re-QA) | Action | T{i+1}? |
|---|---|---|
| `compliant` (first QA) | Extras, append `complete` line | Yes |
| non-compliant on first QA | Exactly one fix pass + re-QA; if A2 still has a confirmed blocker, the Repair round and then the ladder in `refs/retry.md` take over | No |
| `compliant` after that one fix | Extras, append `complete` line | Yes |
| a terminal `halt` (`refs/retry.md`): the ladder did not run after the fix pass, or it stopped | HALT `E-HALT-QA`. Print ledger path, Ti, verdict, missing citations. Next: `fix` \| `ruling` \| `resume` | No, unless operator Ruling |
| clear user confirmation of the explained scoped acceptance, or valid existing operator Ruling | Executor records the Ruling per `refs/ledger.md`; then appends `complete` with **unchanged** non-compliant verdict and fields | Yes |
| `--force`, missing/ambiguous confirmation, or executor-invented approval | STOP `E-NO-RULING` | No |
| `E-RESUME-NEEDED` (`refs/retry.md`) | re-run the same command; do not write a Ruling | No |

Under the Verdict owner rule a non-compliant verdict comes only from a confirmed blocking finding or from a non-finding `cannot-verify` step of the order (zero citations, empty diff, `nogit` with no written-path list); both keep the route of the row "non-compliant on first QA" (that row hands a confirmed blocker after A2 to the Repair round in `refs/retry.md`).

A Ruling counts only when it is eligible under the Ruling eligibility rule in `refs/retry.md`. A clear user confirmation in the current conversation is sufficient; the user need not hand-write a ledger record. Before asking, explain the task id, unmet AC/finding and current outcome, proposed acceptance, reason and cost-if-wrong. A reply such as "yes, accept T2 as explained" authorizes only that explained scope. If confirmation or scope is unclear, ask one targeted question and keep the task blocked. Silence, a generic request to continue, another agent's message, and approval of a different task are not acceptance.

The executor MUST automatically append the existing three-field Ruling, identifying the accepted task/finding and quoting or referencing the user's confirmation in `<what>`, using the reason and cost already explained. Flush it before appending the unchanged non-compliant `complete` line or proceeding. Never invent approval, rewrite history, or mark an accepted gap `compliant`. Existing operator-written records remain valid. A reopened task or changed accepted finding/outcome requires new scoped acceptance; durable records support resume, not guesses from prior chat.

```
T<id>: Ruling: <what, including user confirmation provenance> — <why> — <cost-if-wrong>
```

## Interruption table per attempt

| Attempt | May fail the attempt | May halt | May prompt the user | Minors may be edited |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `blocking` only | `blocking` only (in practice never: an A1 failure goes to the A2 fix pass) | `blocking` only (in practice never) | only inside lines already changed for a blocker |
| A2 with its one repair | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | only inside lines already changed for a blocker |
| A3 | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | no, recorded only |
| A4 | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | `blocking` only | no, recorded only |
| A5 | `blocking` only | `blocking` only (`ladder-end`) | `blocking` only | no, recorded only |
| legacy FINAL | `blocking` only, advisory (never reopens a task) | never | never (summary only) | no |
| managed FINAL | `blocking` only (`issues`) | `blocking` only (`E-ARCHIVE-BLOCKED`) | `blocking` only | no |

Mapping: high = any confirmed checklist `yes` = `blocking`; medium, IMPORTANT without a `yes`, low-medium, low and cosmetic = `minor` or `note`. Every minor and note is recorded in the notes file and cleared: no halt, no Ruling, no user prompt, at every row. "Cleared" means recorded and closed, not necessarily edited. The FINAL still runs. The only non-finding interrupts are the STOP rows of the STOP table in `SKILL.md` (see "Closed list of interrupts" below).

## Closed list of interrupts

Each line names the path, when it fires and why it stays.

1. `E-HALT-QA` after a ladder halt (`ladder-end`, `advice-rejected`, `no-runner-up`, `brief-invalid`, `budget`, `batch`, `no-snapshot`, `head-moved`, `no-evidence`): reachable only after an attempt failed on a confirmed blocker that a repair could not close. Kept because a real failure must block and the revert guards protect data. The halt message and any Ruling request list blocking findings only.
2. `dispute` halt: only when the adviser disputes a blocking finding or the AC itself. Kept because a disputed AC is a user decision.
3. `E-NO-RULING`: reachable only when someone tries to continue past a non-compliant verdict, which now exists only with a blocker. Kept as the user-acceptance safety gate.
4. `operator-review`: user-initiated after a halt, never started by automation.
5. `E-RESUME-NEEDED` (`reviewer-down` after a second paperwork-only or unparseable review, `ref-failed` including a notes file that cannot be written, incomplete revert, adviser agent missing): infrastructure, never about a finding; it asks the user to re-run, not to fix anything. Kept because continuing would record an unverified completion or risk data loss.
6. Input and integrity STOPs (`E-NO-SOURCE`, `E-SOURCE-MISSING`, `E-NO-TASKS`, `E-NO-AC`, `E-LEGACY`, `E-LEDGER-CORRUPT`, `E-LEDGER-PATH`, `E-MANAGED-INVALID`, `E-MANAGED-CONFLICT`, `E-MANAGED-REVIEW-FAIL`, `E-PLAN-CHANGED`, `E-ARCHIVE-MARKER`): occur before or outside per-task QA. Kept unchanged.
7. `E-ARCHIVE-BLOCKED` (managed): FINAL `issues` naming a blocking defect at the end state (see "FINAL derived test" below), `--skip-final-review` on a managed package, or a helper refusal. Kept because FINAL is never waived.

No other path may stop automation or prompt the user. Every halt message and Ruling request lists blocking findings only. A minors-only replay writes no `halt` and no `Ruling:` line.

## FINAL derived test

This is the single statement for both FINALs (the managed archive FINAL and the legacy Whole-list review).

- Both FINALs read the notes, probe, prompt and review files in `<retries>/T<id>/`, apply the severity test of "## Severity model" with the anchor Read-back to the end state, and return `issues` only for a blocking defect. The legacy FINAL applies the same test and stays advisory.
- A notes entry whose answers are all `no` is cited `noted` and is not an unmet AC; a notes entry with a confirmed `yes` is `issues` even when its line labels it minor.
- History: a blocking line of a `review-*.md` that a later status line or a later repair file marks `resolved`, and a notes line prefixed `superseded `, is history, as is every file under `superseded-prompts/` (a moved saved prompt, which FINAL does not compare with the template). FINAL judges the end state, not those lines.
- Saved prompts: line 1 of every saved prompt `prompt-<k>-<j>.md` is the task's start sha, and FINAL compares the lines after the start-sha header and outside the slots with the reviewer template. A prompt that differs only in blank lines or trailing whitespace (their number or position) is not a template difference: record it as a note (cited `noted`), not `issues`. Any changed, added, removed or reordered non-blank line is `issues` (managed) or recorded in `FINAL:` evidence (legacy), as before.
- Superseded prompts: FINAL returns `issues` (managed) or records it in `FINAL:` evidence (legacy) when a superseded prompt's task has no later saved prompt (a higher `j` of the same `k`) in `<retries>/T<id>/` that passes the saved-prompt comparison above, or when that task has no `complete` line after the `FINAL:` line that flagged the prompt (a re-review blocker is recorded in the `FINAL:` evidence instead), or when the `superseded-prompts/` folder has no `README.md`.
- The legacy FINAL trigger depends on task status, not on the verdict value, so the accepted-minor path leaves it unchanged. The accepted-minor path writes no `FINAL:` or `ARCHIVE:` line. For N=1 there is no legacy FINAL; that is existing behaviour, not a waiver.

Residual risk, stated: the FINAL is defence in depth only. Legacy N=1 runs and `--skip-final-review` runs get no FINAL re-check of the notes. The primary gate against a misgraded finding is the mechanical derivation and the anchor Read-back; for those runs the final summary prints every recorded minor.

## Isolation (fail the rewrite if violated)

- Reviewer instructions include: `Do not trust the implementer's report.`
- Reviewer input includes the task brief and the diff, not extras results.
- Same verdict schema whether inline or one Task subagent.

## Managed FINAL review (archive gate)

Same isolation as above: `Do not trust the implementer's report.` One fresh subagent per archive attempt (never inline, even N=1; never reused from an earlier attempt). Input: the current full plan, the full ledger, and the current contents of every delivery file the helper's `--print-state` lists, plus the plan's `## Constraints`. Output: `pass` or `issues` with `path:line` evidence per task AC, taken from the current files and the package's `./artifacts/` logs, not copied from the ledger; reading those logs is the one exception to the Isolation rule above. A per-task `evidence=` line number is a pointer recorded when that task was reviewed, and a later task can move it, so a moved line number alone is never `issues`. `issues` when an AC is unmet at the end state, no evidence for it can be found in the current files or logs, a later change contradicts it, a plan `## Constraints` item is violated, or a log cited on a task's latest `complete` line shows a failure at its outcome line. For a user-accepted gap, verify the current outcome matches the recorded scoped acceptance, cite the unmet AC honestly, and return `issues` for any new or changed unaccepted gap. Never mark unmet AC as met. This pass never rewrites per-task verdicts and is not a code-quality ensemble; the closed per-task verdict grammar is unchanged. The FINAL also reads every brief named by a `retry … step=revert` record and every file in `<retries>/T<id>/` and in `superseded-prompts/`, and judges WHAT against the plan; the forbidden-read rule of the Subagent prompt section never applies to the FINAL. The FINAL prompt also carries the four codegraph run-state fields `index_state`, `checked_at`, `worktree_root` and `projectPath` from the Wave 0 check, with the same standing line as the `{diff}` slot block; it calls codegraph only when `index_state: fresh`. Procedure: `refs/managed-workspace.md`.

## Subagent prompt (when not inline)

Inline when **all** are true: N≤3, source file ≤400 lines, session not compacted, and the review is the first in-flow review of A1 or A2. Else one Task. If compacted mid-run, remaining QA uses the subagent. Once a run switches to subagent mode it stays there; reviews of A3-A5, re-run reviews and operator reviews are always subagents.

An inline review may complete a task only with zero findings and only when the task's notes file holds no line after line 1 (earlier failing reviews append their minors there). An inline review whose findings, or the notes file, would let the task complete with any minor or note is discarded and re-run once as a fresh Task subagent with the closed template below and a saved `prompt-<k>-<j>.md`. Every repair re-review is a fresh subagent.

Every review, inline or subagent, uses this one closed template. The orchestrator fills only the seven slots, from the sources named below, and may not add, remove or reword any criterion, whether it comes from an output style, the session or its own judgment. Inline reviews use the same template text.

```
Review one task for spec compliance.

Task brief: {task_brief}
Global constraints: {global_constraints}
Start sha: {start_sha}
Diff against the start snapshot: {diff}
Delta diff from the previous reviewed tree (empty on the first review): {delta_diff}
Earlier blocking findings of this start (empty on the first review): {prior_findings}
Saved-probe re-check hit locations (may be empty): {recheck_list}

Do not trust the implementer's report.

First mark each earlier blocking finding resolved, open or regressed from the diff. Then, for each AC, mark it met or unmet. Require citations: every AC you mark, met or unmet, carries a `path:line` or `Ti.ACk@path:line` citation, and an unmet mark lists the finding ids behind it. file.content:
# Augment Poll (C2) — the poller contract

This ref pins the poll surface and timing for the SKILL's attended, in-session poll loop. The poll **script**
(`scripts/poll-augment-review.sh`) performs a single `gh`/`gh api` poll and emits one JSON line; the
**FSM** (`superclaude.pr_submit`) does the backoff arithmetic. The script name is kept, but **one
snapshot serves both reviewers** (Augment and Codex): the same reviews, comments and threads are
classified twice, once per reviewer adapter, on the same `expected_head`. This split keeps `gh` out of the
deterministic core (NFR-6) — the script touches `gh`, the core decides.

> Every `gh`/`gh api` call below pins the RESOLVED `--repo <owner/repo>` (origin's `owner/repo`,
> parsed from `git remote get-url origin`; FR-1.3 / AC-7). A bare `gh` without `--repo` is a defect.

## Poll surfaces (FR-2.1)

The adapter obtains PR metadata, then separately paginates formal reviews and both comment sources:

```bash
gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json number,url,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName
gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/reviews --method GET -F per_page=100 -F page=1
gh api repos/<owner/repo>/issues/<N>/comments --method GET -F per_page=100 -F page=1
gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/comments --method GET -F per_page=100 -F page=1
```

REST page numbers advance until a page has fewer than 100 records. Reviews preserve `id`, `commit_id`,
`submitted_at`, `state`, `body`, `user`. `comments` merges raw issue and inline comments (including
`pull_request_review_id`, nullable `line`/`original_line` when supplied); issue comments retain the
legacy decline surface; they also carry the Codex summary comment (its `codex-review-state:v1`
marker and `updated_at`). The configured `augmentcode[bot]` and `augmentcode` identities are unchanged;
the Codex identities are `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` (REST) and `chatgpt-codex-connector` (GraphQL).
No check-run fetch is implemented here; an absent check run is not completion evidence.

The repo-pinned GraphQL query uses `reviewThreads(first:100,after:$endCursor)` with
`pageInfo{hasNextPage endCursor}` and `headRefOid` on **every page**. `threads` contains raw nodes:
`id`, `path`, nullable `line`/`originalLine`, `isResolved`, `isOutdated`, and
`comments(first:1){nodes{...}}`. Only the root is intentionally requested, not a truncated conversation.
Root fields include `id`, `databaseId`, `body`, `path`, nullable `line`/`originalLine`, `createdAt`,
`author{login}`, `replyTo{databaseId}` and `pullRequestReview{id databaseId commit{oid}}`.
Replies cannot create extra findings or turn a human-rooted conversation into an Augment finding.

## Snapshot and classification contract

One JSON line carries `pr`, `url`, `base`, `head_sha`, `observed_at`, `reviews`, `comments`, `threads`,
`reviews_ok`, `comments_ok`, `threads_ok`, and advisory `state` (`review_present` / `polling`).
`observed_at` is the snapshot's UTC timestamp, emitted after collection. The pure core rejects review
submission times later than this observation, without reading a live clock. On initial fetch failure,
the script emits an incomplete event with null head and all flags false (no successful observation).

- `reviews_ok`: complete validated REST reviews; `comments_ok`: **both** REST comment sources;
  `threads_ok`: complete validated GraphQL thread pages.
- API failure, GraphQL `errors` even at exit zero, null connections, malformed pages, missing or
  repeated/nonadvancing cursors, duplicate IDs, or reaching the 1000-page-per-source cap makes that
  source incomplete. Temporary-file staging keeps large payloads out of command arguments.
- The adapter checks head agreement on thread pages and re-reads `headRefOid` after all requests.
  A changed/unreadable final head makes **all three flags false**. During a pushed-SHA wait the
  SKILL must additionally require `payload.head_sha == pushed_sha` **before** the explicit head
  override: a later, internally consistent snapshot may already describe somebody else's push.
- Use `classify(payload, contract, watermark=watermark, current_head_sha=expected_head)` and then
  `actionable_finding_comments` with the **same payload and context**, followed by
  `finding_from_comment` (exported from `severity_router` and the package). Never dispatch raw REST
  comments independently. The SKILL snapshot gate converts empty `findings` selections (possible
  for legacy `has_findings`) or normalization `ValueError` to `polling`, not empty-driver clean.

Cosmos requires all three flags literally true plus validated completion and thread data; explicit
false flags also block legacy classification. Missing additive flags are supported only for legacy
injected payloads, not live Cosmos snapshots. The four core states are `polling`, `clean`, `findings`,
`declined`. `declined` still requires both configured regexes on an Augment-authored entry, strictly
newer than the watermark when supplied; only a valid attributable re-review overrides that decline.
Metadata validation and historical unresolved-root/count rules are in `detection-contract.md`.
Incomplete or invalid evidence remains `polling` under the existing finite timeout: no automatic fix,
round increment or `terminal_clean`.

The advisory `state` (`review_present` only when `reviews_ok`, `comments_ok` and `threads_ok` are all
true and at least one formal review exists; otherwise `polling`) is an Augment-era hint only;
it is not used for Codex, whose completion is the `codex-review-state:v1` marker
(`detection-contract.md`). Codex is classified with `classify_codex` and `codex_finding_comments` on
the same payload and context.

## Two reviewers: wait outcomes and the merge

Each poll gives each reviewer a **wait outcome**: `pending`, `done`, `absent` or `incomplete`.

| Wait outcome | Augment (`augment_wait_outcome(state, nxt, absent=..., marker_defect=...)`) | Codex (`codex_wait_outcome(...)`) |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | `polling` and `poll_outcome` is `S2_CLASSIFY` or `S5C_SILENCE_REREQUEST` | gate state not `clean` / `findings` (still `polling`), and either active and before `--timeout`, or inactive, before the silence deadline and Augment not settled |
| `done` | gate state `clean` / `findings` / `declined` | gate state `clean` / `findings` |
| `absent` | `TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE`, or already absent | inactive when Augment has settled or at the silence deadline, or already absent |
| `incomplete` | `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` (partial activity), or gate state `polling` with a `settled` `marker_defect` (the newest Augment review of the expected head has an unreadable Cosmos marker and is 60 s old; see `detection-contract.md`, "Unreadable marker") | active, gate state still `polling` at `--timeout` |

A reviewer already recorded absent (`rebuild_state()["absent_reviewers"]`), or one whose identity set
is empty, is `absent` at once and is never `pending`. `merge_wait((augment_wait, augment_state),
(codex_wait, codex_state))` maps the pair to one round outcome:

| Augment | Codex | Round outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | any | keep polling |
| any | `pending` | keep polling |
| `done: declined` | any settled | `declined` (S5b fallback; Codex `findings` join its single re-entry) |
| `done` | `done` | `findings` if either has findings, else `clean` |
| `done` | `absent` / `incomplete` | Augment's state (Codex incomplete is reported) |
| `absent` / `incomplete` | `done` | Codex's state (Augment's condition is reported) |
| `absent` | `absent` | `no_response` → `TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE` (no configured reviewer responded) |
| `incomplete` | `absent` / `incomplete` | `timeout` → `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` |
| `absent` | `incomplete` | `timeout` → `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT` (partial reviewer activity, no classified review) |

Both reviewers share the one `--timeout` wall clock and `--poll-interval`; no second wait is added.

**Codex absence rule.** Codex posts its summary comment seconds after a PR opens, so a connected
repository shows Codex activity within the first polls. Codex with no activity when Augment's wait
outcome is settled, or by the silence deadline, is absent: append `reviewer_absent{reviewer:
"codex"}` and ignore Codex for the rest of the run (no wait, no re-trigger). There is no Codex silence
poke. When Augment's silence outcome fires while Codex is present, append `reviewer_absent{reviewer:
"augment"}` and continue with Codex. An Augment-only PR therefore waits no longer than before and adds
only one `reviewer_absent` event.

## Interval, timeout, backoff (FR-2.3 / FR-2.5 / NFR-2)

- **Interval ≥ 30s.** A value below 30 is **rejected, not rounded** ("minimum is 30 seconds", T-111).
- **Timeout default 600s** (~10 min), configurable; **wall-clock since entering wait** (T-221/T-222).
- **Silence window default 300s** (`--silence-timeout`, min 30, clamped to `--timeout`). Zero
  Augment-attributed review/comment (`has_augment_activity` false) is Augment's
  `TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE` outcome (its wait outcome `absent`), not `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT`; the run
  ends there only when Codex is absent too (merge table above). The same deadline is the Codex
  absence deadline. Partial activity (summary/comment but no classified review) still times out
  as `TERMINAL_TIMEOUT`. L3 may consider one poke: pass `rerequested=` / `rerequested_at=` from
  `rebuild_state()`, then `check_idempotent("silence_rerequest_invoked")` → append
  `{event_type: silence_rerequested, pr_number, elapsed}` → `retrigger-review.sh --body "augment review"`.
- **Exponential backoff on 403 / 429 / secondary-limit:** `30 → 60 → 120 → … → cap 300s`, resetting
  on a successful poll (T-231). The backoff **counts toward the wall-clock timeout**.

## Division of labour (the NFR-6 seam)

- The **poll script** assembles ONE snapshot (multiple paginated requests), not a classification.
  Its advisory `state` is not an FSM outcome. It owns no retry/backoff state.
- The **FSM** owns the backoff arithmetic (which interval to use next, whether the cap or the timeout
  is reached) and the state transitions. This keeps the `gh` I/O isolated to the script and the
  deterministic decisions in `superclaude.pr_submit` (NFR-6). The ref explicitly assigns the backoff
  arithmetic to the FSM, never the script.

# Detection Contract (DET) — baked reviewer identities (Augment, Codex)

This ref holds the **default detection contract** for the two review bots: the Augment Code GitHub
App and the ChatGPT Codex Connector (Codex).
The YAML is **configuration, not a parser implementation**. The pure core owns marker validation,
completion attribution and root selection; the configured identities and decline regexes parameterize
it. `classify(payload, contract, *, watermark=None, current_head_sha=None)` returns exactly
`polling` / `clean` / `findings` / `declined`; it never embeds a literal bot login.

Arming does **not** require a local lock file or R1 probe. `DetectionContract.for_arming()`
loads this shipped contract (or an optional gitignored override at
`.dev/pr-monitor/detection-contract.locked.md` when present). A missing/unlocked override
is not a halt.

```yaml
# detection-contract.md — shipped defaults; optional local override may replace these
augment_bot_login: "augmentcode[bot]"                # REST bot-login shape
augment_author_association: ["NONE", "CONTRIBUTOR"]  # observed associations of the Augment author
augment_app_slug: "augmentcode"                      # GraphQL app-slug shape; accepted with bot login
emission_shape: "review"                             # documentary; classifier unused
findings_locus: "comments[]"                         # documentary; classifier unused
severity_field_path: null                            # Augment's self-reported severity, if any (hint only)
review_completeness_signal: "state==COMMENTED"       # documentary
probe_evidence: null                                 # optional provenance; not an arming gate
# V1.1 decline-detection (addendum §6.2 / FR-9.1) — baked defaults; both regexes must match an
# Augment-authored comment for a "declined". accepted_trigger_phrases = our operator re-trigger tokens.
decline_phrase_regex: 'abnormally\s+large'
decline_retrigger_regex: 'comment\s+["''`*_]*(augment|auggie|augmentcode)\s+review["''`*_]*'
accepted_trigger_phrases: ["auggie review", "augment review", "augmentcode review"]
# Codex (ChatGPT Codex Connector) reviewer. An override that omits these keys keeps the
# shipped values; setting BOTH identities to "" disables Codex.
codex_bot_login: "chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]"      # REST bot-login shape
codex_app_slug: "chatgpt-codex-connector"            # GraphQL login shape
codex_retrigger_phrase: "@codex review"              # documented Codex re-review trigger
locked: true                                         # vestigial; arming does not check this flag
```

`augment_author_association`, `emission_shape`, `findings_locus`, `severity_field_path`,
`review_completeness_signal`, and `probe_evidence` are documentary fields, not runtime parser rules.
Changing them does not add a provider, change finding selection or make `state==COMMENTED` sufficient
for Cosmos completion. Identity/decline configuration remains separate from the validation below.

## Cosmos evidence and selection

The `<!-- cosmos-review-status:v1 {JSON} -->` marker is an **observed integration format, not a stable
public API**. The core accepts one bounded v1 marker (JSON object, no duplicate keys), nonempty
`specialist`, `status: reviewed`, full 40-character hexadecimal `head` and `baseline`, and a
nonnegative integer `unresolved_count` (booleans excluded). `session_url` is diagnostic data only.
Malformed/duplicate/unsupported markers, unknown statuses and recognizable Cosmos evidence without
a valid marker cannot fall back to legacy clean. Summary prose and absent checks prove nothing.

**Unreadable marker** (`augment_marker_defect(payload, contract, *, watermark=None, current_head_sha=None)`;
issues #382, #456). Augment sometimes posts a marker that is not valid JSON (PR 377 review 5776522857 and
PR 455 reviews 5819041100 and 5819088356 end `..." -->` with the closing `}` missing). The strict parse
stays: such a review is never clean, never counts as complete and hides nothing, so `classify` is still
`polling`. Option 2 of #456 (accept a marker with a missing brace) is **not** taken: the marker is the only
evidence of `head` and `unresolved_count`, and a guessed repair could turn a truncated body into a false
clean. The helper only *names* the case. It returns a defect when the snapshot is complete, `classify` is
`polling`, and the **newest** formal Augment review of the expected head (submitted no later than
`observed_at`, strictly newer than a `watermark`) has the Cosmos token exactly once and a marker that cannot
be read: `marker_not_valid_json` (invalid JSON or duplicate key), `marker_not_an_object`, or
`marker_comment_unreadable` (token without a closing `-->`, over 8192 bytes, or another marker version).
Valid JSON with wrong fields (for example an in-progress `status`), two tokens, no token, another head, a
non-Augment author or an older-than-watermark review are not defects and poll as before. The result carries
`reason`, `review_id`, `submitted_at`, `settled`, `grace_seconds` (60) and `open_threads` (the comment ids
of that review's open Augment roots, `[]` when none, `None` when they cannot be selected safely).

Policy: report the reason on the first poll that returns a defect. A corrected review can follow within
seconds (PR 455: malformed 18:29:51Z, well formed 18:30:18Z, same head), so the Augment wait stays `pending`
until the unreadable review is 60 s old at `observed_at` (`settled`), then is `incomplete` (at most two polls
at the 30 s minimum interval) instead of waiting for `--timeout`. When monitoring starts after the review is
already 60 s old, `settled` is true on the first poll and nothing more is waited for (the report says so).
`reviewer_incomplete{reviewer: "augment", reason: "marker_malformed", detail}` is recorded whatever the round
outcome is: the run continues with Codex alone, or, when Codex is absent, ends as `timeout` after that event,
with the reason in the report. The operator reads `open_threads` by hand. A later readable review of the same
head is still accepted by the unchanged `classify`.

`current_head_sha` defaults to `payload.head_sha`; an explicit argument **overrides** it. During a
pushed-SHA wait the caller must first check actual `payload.head_sha == pushed_sha`. The selected
latest relevant bot review is ordered by trustworthy submission time, not array order; marker head,
expected head and each provided review commit association must agree. Pending/newer invalid evidence
or ambiguous/missing times cannot be bypassed by an older clean review. Completion must be strictly
newer than `watermark` and no later than `observed_at` (the poll snapshot UTC observation, not a live
clock read in the pure core). Wrong-head-only evidence polls. Contextual legacy reviews also require
head/commit and submission attribution; context-free legacy injected payloads remain supported.

Live Cosmos snapshots require `reviews_ok`, `comments_ok`, `threads_ok` all literally true and complete
review/comment/thread collections. Selection uses unresolved **Augment-rooted** threads, not replies:
resolved roots are excluded even with integer current lines; older outdated-but-unresolved roots
survive a new baseline and the watermark. Their nullable current `line`, `original_line` hint,
`comment_id` (root database ID), `thread_id`, `review_id` and `is_outdated` pass through normalization.
Null current line is not evidence of resolution or a grounded defect.

A root must be created no later than completion. For root selection, completion is the later of the
completed review's submission time and the `createdAt` of the reviewer's own roots whose
`pullRequestReview` is that review (same review id, same commit): GitHub can stamp a review's comments
a second after the review itself (PR 337: review 21:22:29Z, root 21:22:30Z; PR 377: review 21:44:59Z,
root 21:45:00Z, issue #381), and those roots are part of the review, not a sign of a newer one. The rule
is by ownership, not a time gap: there is no allowed number of seconds. A root created after that
completion by any other review, or a root of an older head, still keeps the gate `polling`, and the
re-trigger watermark check is unchanged (a review not strictly newer than the watermark is never the answer
to that re-trigger). The same rule applies to Codex roots under its formal head reviews.

`unresolved_count` is a conservative **lower bound** on required usable detail, not equality with all
historical unresolved threads: positive count with insufficient roots stays polling; zero cannot erase
independently observed old open roots. Classification and `actionable_finding_comments` share one
selection decision with identical payload/head/watermark. The SKILL gate handles empty legacy signals
and normalization errors without feeding empty findings to the driver. Existing decline precedence,
finite timeout and autonomy/round gates remain unchanged.

## Codex evidence and selection

Codex is identified by the non-empty members of `{contract.codex_bot_login, contract.codex_app_slug}`
(REST `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, GraphQL `chatgpt-codex-connector`), read from the contract,
never a literal. An override file that omits a Codex key keeps the shipped value; an explicit empty or
null value blanks that one key. Codex is disabled only when the identity set is empty, so to disable
Codex, blank both keys; blanking one leaves the other identity active.

**Completion** (`codex_review_state` / `classify_codex(payload, contract, *, watermark=None,
current_head_sha=None)`): a Codex-authored issue comment carries one bounded
`<!-- codex-review-state:v1 {JSON} -->` marker (JSON object, duplicate keys rejected, as for Cosmos).
It is valid when `code_review.status` is a string, `code_review.commit_sha` is 40 hex and
`code_review.has_any_findings` is a boolean. When several Codex comments carry a valid marker, the
one with the latest `updated_at` is used; two distinct markers with the same latest time stay
`polling`. The review is complete only when `status == "completed"` and `commit_sha` equals the
expected head. The completion time is the later of the marker comment's `updated_at` and the
`submitted_at` of the newest Codex formal review on the expected head (when one exists); both must be
parseable aware times no later than `observed_at`, and with a watermark the completion must be
strictly newer than it. Anything else (running, wrong head, malformed or duplicate-key JSON, missing
time, incomplete snapshot) is `polling`, never clean. `security_review` is ignored.

**Findings** (`codex_finding_comments`): unresolved review threads whose root is Codex-authored, chosen
by the same root rules as Augment (root only, unique ids, `pullRequestReview` with a commit, nullable
current `line`, `original_line` hint, created no later than completion, where the creation of the
roots of a Codex formal review on the expected head extends completion). Resolved threads are
excluded; older unresolved Codex roots stay visible. Each selected root gets `reviewer: "codex"`,
`codex_priority` and the mapped `severity_hint`. Gate state: no completion or an invalid selection →
`polling`; unresolved roots → `findings`; none and `has_any_findings` false → `clean`; none,
`has_any_findings` true and a Codex formal review on the expected head (its threads all resolved) →
`clean`; otherwise `polling`. Codex has no decline state.

**Badge parser** (`parse_codex_priority(body)`): the first non-blank line must hold exactly one
`![P<n> Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P<m>-<colour>...)` image with `n == m` and `n` in 0-3.
Zero or two badges, `P4`, or alt/URL disagreement give `None` (the Medium fail-safe). Colour is not
checked (only P2 yellow has been observed; P0, P1 and P3 colours are UNVERIFIED).

The `codex-review-state:v1` marker and the badge are **observed integration formats, not a stable
public API** (same standing as the Cosmos marker). A marker format change leaves Codex `polling`,
never a false clean (with Codex activity it ends `incomplete` at `--timeout`); a badge format change
gives `None`, the Medium fail-safe.

## Consequences

1. **Identity is configurable (no literal login).** The classifier builds the non-empty identity
   set `{contract.augment_bot_login, contract.augment_app_slug}`, **never** a literal string.
   This accepts REST bot-login shape (`augmentcode[bot]`) and GraphQL app-slug shape
   (`augmentcode`) when both are present in data. A different bot login is treated as
   "review not detected" (T-211). When Augment and human reviews are interleaved, only the
   Augment author is parsed (T-212). The default retrigger regex also matches the live
   `comment "**_augment review_**"` Markdown wrapper while still requiring the separate
   `abnormally\s+large` phrase. Codex identities work the same way
   (`{contract.codex_bot_login, contract.codex_app_slug}`); Codex roots never enter Augment's
   selection, and Augment roots never enter Codex's.

2. **No lock gate.** Arming loads this shipped contract (or an optional local override).
   `locked: false` / a missing override is not a halt. A local override is a refinement,
   not a requisite. One change point on Augment drift: edit the identity fields here
   (or drop a local override) — **no control-flow code changes** (spec §7 consequence 2).

3. **Optional override.** `.dev/pr-monitor/detection-contract.locked.md` is still preferred
   when present (`for_arming()` / `prefer_local_override=True`) so a fork can pin a
   different bot identity without forking the shipped skill.

4. **Purity seam (AC-9 / NFR-6).** No `gh`/`git` token appears in `state-machine.md`,
   `severity-routing.md`, or `loop-guard.md` — protecting the seam from a future maintainer
   inlining a bot-login string. Tested by **T-N50**.

BACKOFF_BASE = MIN_POLL_INTERVAL  # 30s
BACKOFF_CAP = 300  # 5 min


def next_backoff(prev_interval: int) -> int:
    """Next exponential backoff interval: ``30 → 60 → 120 → … → cap 300`` (FR-2.5).

    ``prev_interval <= 0`` (or below base) restarts at the 30s base; otherwise it
    doubles, capped at 300s. A successful poll resets the caller's interval to 0 so
    the next backoff restarts at the base (T-231: backoff 30, 60, reset).
    """
    if prev_interval < BACKOFF_BASE:
        return BACKOFF_BASE
    return min(prev_interval * 2, BACKOFF_CAP)


def timed_out(elapsed_seconds: int, timeout: int) -> bool:
    """Whether the wall-clock timeout has fired (``elapsed >= timeout``, FR-2.3)."""
    return elapsed_seconds >= timeout


def poll_outcome(
    review_state: str,
    elapsed_seconds: int,
    timeout: int,
    *,
    silent: bool = False,
    silence_timeout: int = DEFAULT_SILENCE_TIMEOUT,
    rerequested: bool = False,
    rerequested_at: int | None = None,
    monitor_ordinal: int = 0,
) -> MonitorState:
    """Map a poll result + elapsed time to the next FSM state.

    Positional ``(polling, elapsed, timeout)`` with ``silent=False`` still fires
    ``TERMINAL_TIMEOUT`` (partial-activity timeout, T-221). When ``silent`` is
    true, zero Augment activity uses ``TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE`` and may
    return ``S5C_SILENCE_REREQUEST`` once at L3 before that terminal.
    """
    if review_state in ("clean", "findings"):
        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
    if review_state == "polling" and silent:
        if timed_out(elapsed_seconds, timeout):
            return MonitorState.TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE
        if rerequested:
            if rerequested_at is None:
                return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
            second_deadline = min(rerequested_at + silence_timeout, timeout)
            if elapsed_seconds >= second_deadline:
                return MonitorState.TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE
            return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
        if elapsed_seconds >= silence_timeout:
            if monitor_ordinal >= 3 and elapsed_seconds + MIN_POLL_INTERVAL < timeout:
                return MonitorState.S5C_SILENCE_REREQUEST
            return MonitorState.TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE
        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
    if timed_out(elapsed_seconds, timeout):
        return MonitorState.TERMINAL_TIMEOUT
    return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# transition() — the transition table (spec §5.4: a table, not nested ifs)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def transition(
    state: MonitorState, event: str, context: dict | None = None
) -> MonitorState:
    """Return the next state for ``(state, event)`` under the ordinal ceiling.

    The ``needs_human_decision`` override is evaluated FIRST (pre-gate, §5.2): any
    event in a cycle carrying ``needs_human_decision`` routes to HALT_HUMAN
    regardless of ordinal. Otherwise the edge is looked up in the transition table,
    with the three ordinal gates applied at their edges.
    """
    ctx = context or {}
    ordinal = int(ctx.get("monitor_ordinal", 0))

    # Pre-gate override (the ONLY ceiling short-circuit).

WAIT_INCOMPLETE = "incomplete"
_DONE_STATES = (STATE_CLEAN, STATE_FINDINGS, STATE_DECLINED)


def _state_name(value: Any) -> str:
    return str(getattr(value, "value", value))


def augment_wait_outcome(
    state: str,
    next_state: Any,
    *,
    absent: bool = False,
    marker_defect: dict | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Augment's wait outcome from the existing gate state and ``poll_outcome`` result.

    ``absent`` (already recorded absent, or no Augment identity) is ``absent`` at
    once and is never ``pending`` (A2). ``marker_defect`` is the result of
    :func:`~superclaude.pr_submit.classifier.augment_marker_defect`: while the gate is
    ``polling`` and that defect is ``settled`` (the unreadable review is past its grace
    window), the wait is ``incomplete`` now instead of ``pending`` until ``--timeout``.
    It never turns into ``done``, so an unreadable marker is never a clean review.
    """
    if absent:
        return WAIT_ABSENT
    if state in _DONE_STATES:
        return WAIT_DONE
    if (
        state == STATE_POLLING
        and isinstance(marker_defect, dict)
        and marker_defect.get("settled") is True
    ):
        return WAIT_INCOMPLETE
    nxt = _state_name(next_state)
    if nxt == "TERMINAL_AUGMENT_NO_RESPONSE":
        return WAIT_ABSENT
    if nxt == "TERMINAL_TIMEOUT":
        return WAIT_INCOMPLETE
    return WAIT_PENDING


def codex_wait_outcome(
    state: str,
    *,
    active: bool,
    elapsed: int,
    timeout: int,
    silence_timeout: int,
    other_settled: bool,
    absent: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Codex's wait outcome.

    ``absent`` (already recorded absent, or no Codex identity) is ``absent`` at once
    (A2). A Codex with no activity is absent as soon as Augment is settled or at the
    silence deadline; an active Codex with no completion is ``incomplete`` at
    ``--timeout``.
    """
    if absent:
        return WAIT_ABSENT
    if state in (STATE_CLEAN, STATE_FINDINGS):
        return WAIT_DONE
    if active:
        return WAIT_INCOMPLETE if elapsed >= timeout else WAIT_PENDING
    if other_settled or elapsed >= min(silence_timeout, timeout):
        return WAIT_ABSENT
    return WAIT_PENDING


def merge_wait(augment: tuple[str, str], codex: tuple[str, str]) -> dict:
    """Merge per-reviewer ``(wait_outcome, gate_state)`` pairs into one round outcome.

    ``outcome`` is ``polling`` / ``clean`` / ``findings`` / ``declined`` /
    ``no_response`` / ``timeout``; ``used`` names the reviewers whose results the
    outcome uses, ``absent`` / ``incomplete`` the others (design section 6 table).
    """
    pairs = {"augment": augment, "codex": codex}
    absent = [name for name, (out, _) in pairs.items() if out == WAIT_ABSENT]
    incomplete = [name for name, (out, _) in pairs.items() if out == WAIT_INCOMPLETE]
    done = [(name, st) for name, (out, st) in pairs.items() if out == WAIT_DONE]
    result = {
        "outcome": STATE_POLLING,
        "used": [],
        "absent": absent,
        "incomplete": incomplete,
    }
    if any(out == WAIT_PENDING for out, _ in pairs.values()):
        return result
    result["used"] = [name for name, _ in done]
    if augment == (WAIT_DONE, STATE_DECLINED):
        result["outcome"] = STATE_DECLINED
    elif done:
        findings = any(st == STATE_FINDINGS for _, st in done)
        result["outcome"] = STATE_FINDINGS if findings else STATE_CLEAN
    elif len(absent) == len(pairs):
        result["outcome"] = "no_response"
    else:
        result["outcome"] = "timeout"
    return result

# One bounded chunk of the attended poll loop for PR 845. Prints one summary line per poll.
# usage: waitloop.sh <start-epoch> <timeout> <silence> <absent-csv> <chunk-seconds>
set -u
START="$1"; TIMEOUT="$2"; SILENCE="$3"; ABSENT="$4"; CHUNK="$5"
REPO=IronbellyOrg/IronClaude
PR=845
BEGIN=$(date +%s)
cd /home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/issue-842 || exit 3
while true; do
  NOW=$(date +%s)
  ELAPSED=$((NOW - START))
  bash ~/.claude/skills/sc-pr-submit-protocol/scripts/poll-augment-review.sh --pr "$PR" --repo "$REPO" > /tmp/prsub-845/payload.json 2>/tmp/prsub-845/poll.err || { echo "POLL-SCRIPT-FAILED rc=$?"; cat /tmp/prsub-845/poll.err; exit 4; }
  cp /tmp/prsub-845/payload.json /tmp/prsub-845/payload-$ELAPSED.json
  OUT=$(uv run python -I /tmp/prsub-845/gate.py /tmp/prsub-845/payload.json "$ELAPSED" "$TIMEOUT" "$SILENCE" "$ABSENT" 2>&1 | tail -1)
  echo "t=$ELAPSED $OUT" | cut -c1-900
  if echo "$OUT" | grep -q '"outcome": "polling"'; then
    :
  else
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ $(( $(date +%s) - BEGIN )) -ge "$CHUNK" ]; then echo "CHUNK-END elapsed=$ELAPSED"; exit 0; fi

done
